### The 4 sandbox-dependent failures

| Test | Fails here? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **adoption level** (`test_minimal_kernel_passes_at_minimal_level`) | Yes | Node v18.20.8 on PATH, not v22.23.3. Node's registry `install` field (`bash -c '. ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm install 22.23.3'`) has no `PATH=` prefix, so doctor falls back to PATH and finds v18 → tools section fails → doctor unhealthy → assertion `"minimal" in text` fails because result is in `error.details` not `result`. |
| **doctor envelope** (`test_doctor_envelope_is_valid_on_healthy_project`) | Yes | Same root cause — node version mismatch makes doctor unhealthy, envelope has `ok: false`. |
| **doctor read-command** (`test_doctor_is_a_read_command`) | Yes | Doctor exits 3 (DOCTOR_UNHEALTHY) instead of 0, because node v18 ≠ v22. |
| **code index** (`test_rebuild_codeintel_is_recreated_when_tool_answers`) | Yes | Sandbox read-only filesystem: `[Errno 30] Read-only file system: '/tmp/gov-cbm-1000/...'`. Unrelated to my changes. |

---

### Point 2: Which case should have been red, and why

**Case `test_tool_at_registered_location_passes` should have been red.**

Its assertion `"ok" in tools_text` matched the JSON *key* `"ok"` (which appears for every tool) regardless of the boolean value, so it passed even though doctor was NOT using registered locations. The code used only `_find_binary` (PATH + `~/.local/bin/`), never the registry's install path.

**The fix (option a):** The code now extracts a `PATH=<prefix>:$PATH` pattern from each registry entry's `install` field via `_extract_path_prefix()` and checks that directory first, before falling back to PATH.

**Node's registry entry carries no parsable location.** Its `install` is:
```yaml
install: "bash -c '. ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm install 22.23.3'"
```
There is no `PATH=…:$PATH` prefix. The `note` field says `"at ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin/node"` but that's free text. To make doctor find node v22, the registry would need either a `location` field or the install command would need:
```
PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH bash -c '. ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm install 22.23.3'
```

The entries that DO have the prefix and ARE found at their registered locations:
```yaml
# openspec (line ~30)
install: "PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@1.13.2"

# ccusage (line ~45)
install: "PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH $HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin/npm install -g ccusage@20.0.26"
```
